title: Latency-floor evacuation and capacity fences for multi-region steering
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: During regional degradation we need a routing policy that (1) preserves end-user latency SLOs (p99/p95 floors), (2) avoids aggressive global failover that overloads remaining regions, and (3) enables graceful evacuation when a region is degraded. Current steering is reactive and either routes too many requests away (breaking locality and cost targets) or floods healthy regions when capacity is constrained.
background: Recent incidents (see incident-2025-12-03) showed simultaneous partial outages in us-west causing downstream regions to hit saturation within minutes. Existing circuit breakers are coarse (region-level drop rates) and do not consider latency quantiles or customer tokens. Product requires staying within configured SLOs (p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for hosted tier) while minimizing cross-region egress and preserving Dedicated capacity guarantees.
goals: 1) Introduce a latency-floor based evacuation mechanism that only evicts traffic from a region when quantile latency exceeds configured floor for a sustained window. 2) Implement capacity fences: soft credits + hard caps per region to prevent cascade overload. 3) Blend geo-pinning preference with capacity-aware steering so high-affinity customers remain pinned until safe. 4) Expose metrics and Console controls (thresholds, credits) for SRE and customer teams.
non_goals: Replace per-model autoscaling; implement full cross-region cache migration; change pricing models.
design_notes: High-level approach: compute per-region steering signals combining three inputs: latency_signal, capacity_signal, and affinity_score. Latency_signal uses sliding-window quantiles (p95, p99) with outlier damping. Capacity_signal derives from running capacity credits (tokens) replenished by reserve bandwidth and reduced by request cost (tokenized). Affinity_score comes from customer pinning rules and session residency metrics. Decision rule: if latency_signal > latency_floor AND capacity_signal < soft_threshold => begin staged evacuation (drain fraction 10% -> 30% -> 60% over N windows). If capacity_signal < hard_threshold => trigger immediate circuit breaker for non-pinned traffic. Backoff windows, hysteresis, and cooldowns prevent flip-flopping. We will leverage existing admission controller and extend steerbox to accept a prioritization vector.
acceptance_criteria: 1) In canary traffic (10% of production), p95 stays below 120ms and p99 below 300ms during injected degradation while global request rate to other regions does not exceed 110% of baseline. 2) Capacity fences prevent any region from exceeding hard token caps during a synthetic failover. 3) Console shows live per-region credits and latency-floor alerts. 4) Automated test harness reproduces staged evacuation behavior and circuit-breaker activation with deterministic inputs.
tasks: Prototype latency-floor detector using t-digest quantiles (runtime metric pipeline)
Design capacity credits model and integrate with admission-controller token accounting
Implement staged evacuation controller in steerbox; add drain fraction and windows
Add affinity-aware exemptions: allow pinned customers to retain a share until safe
Instrument metrics: per-region p95/p99, credits, drain-state, breaker-state
Create Console controls and graph widgets for ops toggles and thresholds
End-to-end canary and chaos tests using chaos-engine (inject latency + CPU pressure)
Write runbook describing SRE response and rollback steps
risks: 1) Overly aggressive evacuation could increase cross-region egress costs and violate Dedicated SLAs. 2) Quantile computation delay could make decisions lag; need sampling guarantees. 3) Affinity exemptions could starve non-pinned customers. 4) Incorrect token math may produce oscillation between regions.
mitigations: Start with a conservative drain fraction and long windows in canary, add synthetic load tests, monitor fast fail metrics, and provide operator override. Numerical stability: use reservoir sampling with watermarking for quantile streams.

2026-02-05 - Marco Alvarez: Spike complete; prototype computes p95/p99 via t-digest with 30s windows. Observed ~10s computation latency in staging; need to optimize aggregator path.

2026-02-25 - SRE sync: agreed on initial parameters: drain windows = [60s, 180s, 600s], drain fractions = [10,30,60], soft_threshold = 70% credits, hard_threshold = 30% credits. These are conservative and subject to tuning.
